key_insight: Diffusion generation expands accessible ABX₃ perovskite compositions, including ordered double perovskites, but does not establish enrichment near the 1.4 eV bandgap target.
engineering_relevance: The workflow could support photovoltaic absorber screening if generated candidates undergo topology checks, chemistry-aware property validation and first-principles relaxation.
method: Generate candidate ABX₃ structures with a pretrained diffusion model.
Filter for three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskite connectivity.
Evaluate chemistry and ALIGNN-predicted bandgaps; check six structures with first-principles calculations.
evidence_signal: The predicted target-window fraction was 8.2% versus 7.3% for the Materials Project reference, while ALIGNN failed to outperform a constant baseline on a severe B-site-disjoint test.
watch_item: Different conditioning and evaluation label sources limit target-enrichment claims, and relaxation can change structural classification while calculated gaps can differ appreciably from predictions.
paper_title: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX$_3$ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery
